Musopen Symphony (orchestra — Commons page credit), Czech National Symphony Orchestra (orchestra — embedded FLAC credit) Disputed: sources disagree

The display name and the embedded artist tag differ. It is not established whether ‘Musopen Symphony’ is a project credit for this orchestra or a mistaken attribution. No conductor is identified.

Processing
Commons file: 24-bit FLAC; upstream collection description: 32-bit conversion. Disputed: sources disagree

Commons’ file metadata documents a 48 kHz stereo 24-bit FLAC encoded with libFLAC 1.2.1. The Internet Archive’s collection-wide description says 32 bits per sample. The records do not establish whether an intervening conversion explains the difference; no mastering or noise treatment is documented.

  • 24-bit, 48 kHz stereo FLAC in Commons file metadata.
  • 32-bit FLAC conversion claimed in the upstream collection description.
[3] [5]
Composition rights
Commons applies PD-old-auto-expired, with Brahms’s death year 1897. Documented

The tag addresses the musical composition, including its pre-1931 publication basis in the United States; it is separate from the new recording.

[1]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — recording release: PD-author public-domain dedication by Musopen. Documented

Commons explicitly applies PD-author by Musopen to the recording, separately from the composition. This is the programme’s explicit Musopen recording-release route, not an age-based inference or a claim that a Public Domain Mark is itself a licence. The session date is not needed for this route.

[6]
